body.p: CoNLL-O is an implementation of the CoNLL-U Plus Format, as defined by the Universal Dependencies framework.
CoNLL-O provides the standard CoNLL document metadata with some additions. The newdoc ID is a CDLI/Oracc catalogue number.

dl.dd: gives a common name or designation for the document referenced by the newdoc ID. This can be used with the ORACC:LINELABEL field to create human readable labels for word occurrences.
gives the Oracc project for the source data. This can be used in combination with ORACC:WORDID or ORACC:LINEID to create URLs that link to the highlighted word or line.

gives the ATF source file which is the ultimate source of the CoNLL-O data; when CoNLL-O is used for data interchange atffile can be used in combination with the ORACC:ATFLW field to align annotation with the source document.

body.p: CoNLL gives sentences in transliteration because that is the disciplinary practice in Sumerology. The # text entry for a sentence is derived from the XML version of the original ATF file. In addition to the text and translation, CoNLL-O gives each sentence in Sumero-Akkadian cuneiform in the # xsux comment.
CoNLL-O retains the ten core CoNLL-U fields: ID FORM LEMMA UPOS XPOS FEATS HEAD DEPREL DEPS MISC.

The fields FORM and LEMMA are given in transliteration because this is a closer reflection of the surface form of the word than the ePSD2 Citation Form which relies on a Guide Word for disambiguation. Thus, ePSD2's a[water]N and a[arm]N share the Citation Form a; in cuneiform these words are typically written 𒀀 (U+12000) and 𒀉 (U+12009) respectively. In the LEMMA column these words are given as a and a₂ following conventions defined in the Oracc Sign List and the electronic Pennsylvania Sumerian Dictionary. We prefer transliteration rather than cuneiform for LEMMA because cuneiform ideograms are typically used to write more than one word--𒀀 (U+12000) is used for a[water]N and duru₅=duru[wet]V/i, for example.
The extension fields ORACC:FORMC and ORACC:LEMMAC give the corresponding cuneiform.
CoNLL-O field names are in the ORACC namespace.

CoNLL-O adds 14 fields which are identical with the fields contained in Oracc lemmatization signatures, as well as several other fields that are not included in an Oracc signature. The names of these fields are the Oracc signature field name preceded by 'ORACC:': ORACC:LANG ORACC:CF ORACC:GW ORACC:SENSE ORACC:POS ORACC:EPOS ORACC:NORM ORACC:BASE ORACC:CONT ORACC:STEM ORACC:MORPH ORACC:MORPH2.

Note that the FORM field of Oracc signatures is suppressed in CoNLL-O because it would be identical to the CoNLL-U FORM field and is therefore redundant. The PROJECT field of Oracc signatures is also suppressed because that is given in the document header.
The only CoNLL-O signature field that is given in transliteration is ORACC:BASE; there is also a corresponding ORACC:BASEC field that gives the cuneiform for ORACC:BASE.

CoNLL-O includes additional fields that relate words to the electronic Pennsylvania Sumerian Dictionary. In Oracc's internal formats these are not embedded in the signatures but they are available in the XML versions of the annotated data for text editions or glossaries: CoNLL-O ensures that these data are available without recourse to external datasets.

dl.dd: The ORACC:OID is the standard Oracc ID for the word.
The ORACC:SENSEID is the Oracc Sense ID: these are derived from the OID plus a dotted subscript, e.g., o0123456.1, etc. The SENSE IDs will be stabilized with the release of ePSD 2.8.
The CoNLL-U FORM field in Unicode cuneiform.
The CoNLL-U LEMMA field in Unicode cuneiform.
The CoNLL-O BASE field in Unicode cuneiform.

Oracc assigns an XML:ID to each word which consists of the CDLI/ORACC text ID ([PQX][0-9]{,6}) and two dotted subscripts of which the first is the line ID component and the second the word ID component (e.g., P123456.1.1).
Oracc assigns an XML:ID to each line which consists of the CDLI/ORACC text ID ([PQX][0-9]{,6}) and one dotted subscripts giving the line ID component (e.g., P123456.1).
Oracc computes a human-readable label for each line which is guaranteed unique within the document. The label for obverse, column 1, line 1 is 'o i 1'. This column may include space characters.
For interchange purposes, this field gives the line number in the ATF file given in the document header as well as the index of the word in the line, in the format [LINE]/[WORDINDEX], e.g., 123/1.
